readerTitle: Six weeks to change how a store works
caseNote: 가상 사례 (식료품점 온라인 주문 피킹 도입, IT 관리 서비스 회사의 티켓 포털 전환) · 적용 레슨으로 PPL-07-03, PPL-07-04 개념을 사용
insight: 변화를 이끌 때 내 팀에는 '변화 리더십'을, 내 권한 밖의 사람에게는 '권한 없는 영향력'을 쓴다. 두 방법 모두 '이 변화가 상대에게 무엇을 잃게 하는가'를 묻는 데서 출발한다.
misconception: 본사가 결정한 변화는 일정과 지시만 잘 전달하면 된다. 협조하지 않는 다른 부서는 윗선을 통해 밀어붙이면 된다.

sources.text: 이 유닛의 개념 레슨 PPL-07-03 (Leading change), PPL-07-04 (Influence without authority)
모든 사례와 수치(직원 40명, 6주, 오전 7시 등)는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 인물, 매장, 회사, 수치는 설명용 가상 사례입니다. 실제 기업이나 연구 수치를 인용하지 않았습니다.
적용 레슨이므로 새 개념을 소개하지 않았는지, 용어가 PPL-07-03, PPL-07-04 본문의 정의(변화의 이유 제시, 초기 성과, 회의론자 참여 / 상대의 목표 파악, 교환, 약속 이행)와 일치하는지 확인하세요.
트럭 도착 시간 설정(7시 피킹 시작, 6시 도착으로 변경 제안)이 이야기 안에서 서로 맞는지 확인했습니다. 6시에 도착하면 7시 피킹 전에 하역을 마칠 수 있다는 가정입니다.

cards.title: Six weeks to change how a store works
body: Maya runs a busy grocery store. Head office has decided that in six weeks, the store will start picking online orders straight from its own shelves.
Her team of 40 heard about it from a rumor before she could tell them. By Monday, the break room had its own version: *fewer hours, more work, and nobody asked us*.

image.label: Store staff whispering in a break room
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 식료품점 휴게실에서 앞치마를 입은 직원 서너 명이 머리를 맞대고 속삭이고, 문가에 매장 관리자(30대 여성)가 서류를 들고 서 있다. 벽에 '6 weeks' 달력. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your first team meeting
body: You're Maya. You have 15 minutes with each shift before opening. What do you lead with?

options.text: The plan: dates, new roles and the picking schedule
options.feedback: Clear plans are good managing, and people need them. But without a reason and a chance to raise worries, a schedule sounds like a verdict.

options.text: Why it's happening, what stays the same, and what worries them
options.feedback: This is **leading change**: make the case in their terms (weekend shoppers are moving online), say what won't change, and bring fears out early while you can still act on them.

options.text: Head office decided, so there's no point debating it
options.feedback: It's honest and it keeps the blame off you. But it tells the team nobody is steering, which makes the rumor feel truer.

cards.title: The worries were practical.
body: The team didn't fear the idea. They feared the details. Pickers with carts would block the aisles. Morning restocking already ran late. And Tom, the produce lead everyone listened to, called it a fad.

Maya started small: one zone, two pickers, two weeks. She asked Tom to design the picking route through produce, the area he knew best. His route cut walking time, and soon **his own crew was defending it**.

image.label: A picker's route drawn on a store map
image.brief: 매장 평면도 위에 한 구역(채소·과일 코너)만 색칠되어 있고, 손으로 그린 피킹 동선 화살표가 지나간다. 옆에 베테랑 직원이 연필을 들고 동선을 그리는 모습. 로고 없음.

cards.title: The truck arrives at the wrong time.
body: Picking needs to start at 7 a.m. That's exactly when the delivery truck arrives, and unloading takes every free hand.
The delivery schedule is set by the regional warehouse team. You don't manage them.

options.text: Ask your regional boss to order a different delivery time
options.feedback: It might work once. But it spends your boss's authority and teaches the warehouse to see you as a problem. **Influence without authority** lasts longer when you don't borrow rank.

options.text: Ask the warehouse what they struggle with, then offer a trade and a short trial
options.feedback: That's **influence without authority**: learn their goals and offer something they value. Maya learned drivers hated waiting for empty cages, so she offered cages sorted and ready if the truck came at 6.

options.text: Work around it by adding an early shift so both jobs fit
options.feedback: It fixes today's clash, and it's fully in your control. But it adds cost every day and leaves the real cause untouched.

cards.title: Two ideas did the heavy lifting.
body: With her team, Maya used **leading change**: a reason people could believe, an early win they could see, and a real role for the skeptic.
With the warehouse, she had no authority at all. So she used **influence**: she found what they wanted and made her request part of the answer.
The tools differ, but both start with the same question: what does this change cost the other person?

image.label: Two paths: own team and outside team
image.brief: 두 갈래 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 'Your team' 아래에 'A reason', 'An early win', 'A role for skeptics'. 오른쪽 'Outside your authority' 아래에 'Their goals', 'A fair trade', 'Keep your word'. 가운데 공통 질문 'What does it cost them?'. 깔끔한 플랫 스타일.

cards.title: Some losses are real.
body: Not every worry is fear of the new. Two cashiers would lose their afternoon shifts and move to early picking. Calling that an *opportunity* would have cost Maya trust.

Name real losses plainly and soften them where you can, for example by swapping shifts or phasing the change in. And keep your side of every trade. If the cages aren't ready on day three, the warehouse won't listen to your next request.

cards.title: Now it's an IT support firm.
body: Priya manages accounts at a firm that runs IT for 30 small offices. The firm is moving clients from phone support to an online ticket portal, so every request gets tracked.
Clients don't report to her, and many of them like calling. What should she do?

options.text: Announce a date and switch off the phone line
options.feedback: Fast and simple. But it skips the case for change and treats clients as if they worked for you. Expect angry calls to her boss instead.

options.text: Pilot with one office manager who has lost requests before, and keep a phone line for emergencies
options.feedback: Both ideas at work: a believable reason and an early win (**leading change**), plus a respected peer spreading the word (**influence without authority**). The emergency line respects a real loss.

options.text: Let every client choose phone or portal, for good
options.feedback: Nobody gets upset. But the tracking benefit never arrives, and her team runs two systems forever.

cards.title: Lead your team through it. Persuade everyone else.
body: You used two ideas from this unit: **leading change** (a reason, an early win, a role for skeptics) and **influence without authority** (find what others want, offer a fair trade, keep your word).
**Try it today:** pick one change you're planning. List everyone it touches, and next to each name, write what they might lose.
